title: Choose the visual world for Trailmark
question: Your Iceland trip, and every trip after it. Keep the lead direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Postcards Home
options.lineage: Picture postcards and airmail sent home from the road
options.thesis: Each day of the trip arrives as a postcard: your best photo on the front, and the day's story, route and postmark on the back.
options.viewport: On a deep airmail-blue ground sits the bundle of 7 cards. The top card shows the trip's strongest photo (Skógafoss rainbow). Its back peeks out with a postmark reading REYKJAVÍK · 7 DAYS and the whole Ring Road route drawn as the stamp. As you scroll, one card deals off per day.
options.risk: Tips into scrapbook kitsch (fake tape, handwriting fonts) if done timidly. The card borders also limit how big a photo can read on a phone.

raised.raise: Every card back uses the same fixed layout (postmark, stamp box, message, route), so a Taiwan trip slots in with no redesign.
Each day gets one stamp colour, sampled from its hero photo, used everywhere for that day: map leg, nav marker, postmark ink.
Postmarks show real measured facts computed from the route (stops, km driven), never decoration.
The postmark is one form repeated at every scale: huge on the bundle, small as the sticky 'where am I' marker while you scroll.
The island route on the top card is the index: tap a day's leg to jump to its postcard.

options.label: Contact Sheet & Selects
options.lineage: Darkroom contact sheets on a light table
options.thesis: Each day is a roll of film on the light table. Every frame is there; the best ones are circled in grease pencil and printed big.
options.viewport: The whole trip as one sheet: 7 film strips stacked, each day named in film-edge print. One circled frame is blown up full-bleed, and the route is scrawled in grease pencil over a small map.
options.risk: The most familiar photo-centric take on a travelogue, so it's where many runs would land. It can also feel like a photographer's in-joke.

options.label: The Route Ribbon
options.lineage: Museum provenance ribbon, fused with your route
options.thesis: One continuous ribbon (the actual route) runs the full length of the page, folding at every day and every stop.
options.viewport: The ribbon enters at the top as the Ring Road over a faint island outline, then folds into the days with dated small caps. Photos hang off the ribbon at the stop where they were taken; rest days show as loose grey thread.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the route as one line through time and place is the clearest journey story. It loses on warmth, because it reads like a museum record rather than your holiday.
options.risk: Buff paper plus serif type is a well-worn look, and it can feel archival and cold.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: The trip as a departures board, with each day a row that flips in as you arrive.
options.viewport: A board listing DAY 1 to DAY 7 with destinations, cascading as you scroll.
options.case: Great as an index, but the board can't hold photos, and photos are the whole point.
options.kept: Fixed fields on every card back.
options.risk: Becomes a header gimmick over a generic gallery.

options.label: Arcade Pixel Glow
options.thesis: The trip as a pixel overworld, one screen per day.
options.viewport: A pixel-art island map with a car sprite on the Ring Road.
options.case: Fun, but fat pixels fight real photographs and the couple's keepsake tone.
options.kept: A strict colour per day, used everywhere.

options.label: Annotated Dress Code
options.thesis: Photos annotated with leader-line callouts and measured rules.
options.viewport: A hero photo with callouts naming each place.
options.case: Precise but clinical; friends don't recognise themselves in it.
options.risk: Feels like a diagram, not a trip.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Place names set in coarse pixel type at poster scale.
options.viewport: HVERAGERÐI in giant pixels over dense columns.
options.case: Type-led, while this content is photo-led.
options.kept: One form repeated at every scale.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Layout follows a network of forces instead of a grid.
options.viewport: A floating strut diagram linking the days.
options.case: No real link to a road trip.
options.kept: The route network is the navigation.

canonCard.label: Classic photo essay
canonCard.thesis: The standard scrolly travel story, done at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed hero photo with a big title, then a sticky map beside alternating photo and text sections per day.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other travel blog by design.
